title: Window Contraction Fairness Probe Journal
content:
Purpose:
This is a working journal for an exploratory set of experiments we call 'window contraction' — a dynamic mechanism that gradually reduces the batch-formation window for latency-sensitive requests while preserving fairness and throughput for bulk workloads. Goal is to find stable contraction heuristics that cut 95th/99th tail without regressing throughput or starving low-priority tenants.

Background / motivation:
- Continuous batchers currently use a fixed/timeout-driven coalescing window. That often creates a tension: increasing window helps throughput but worsens tail latency for urgent small requests; decreasing window reduces throughput and increases per-token cost.
- Previous experiments focused on static hybrid windows and urgency-weighted batching. This probe tries a different axis: contract the window as a function of per-slot urgency pressure and recent tail measurements, with a soft refill to avoid oscillation.

Hypotheses:
1) A gentle contraction curve (window *= 0.7 when 95th latency exceeds threshold) will reduce tail latency for urgent requests within 1–2ms median loss, while preserving >95% of throughput for steady load.
2) If contraction triggers are tied to per-cohort latency (not global), we avoid cross-tenant unfair demotions.
3) Rapid contraction followed by exponential backoff introduces oscillation and hurts throughput; add hysteresis and reopen gates slowly.

Experiment design:
- Surface: continuous-batcher v2 (local branch: window-contract-probe).
- Scenarios: mixed traffic (60% background large requests avg tokens=120, 40% interactive short requests avg tokens=16). Traffic replay recorded from 2024-11 production window.
- Metric buckets: P50/P95/P99 latency (request completion), tokens/sec, model GPU utilization, small-request wait-time distribution, batch size distribution per slot, per-tenant fairness index (Jain’s index computed on service rate).
- Arms: control (fixed window 6ms), contraction-soft (window = base * 0.9 on single-trigger, 0.7 on repeated triggers with hysteresis), contraction-aggressive (window halves immediately when P95 > 60ms), cohort-aware contraction (contract only for slots dominated by interactive cohort).
- Duration: 2-hour runs each, three repeats.

Instrumentation changes added for these runs:
- Event annotations for every window-change (timestamped, reason, prior-window, new-window, cohort-id).
- Per-slot cohort dominance score logged (0..1).
- Moving-window tail-estimator: EWMA of P95 with alpha=0.2, kept per-slot and global.
- Added counter for 'contraction-churn' increments each time window grows/shrinks; tracked to detect oscillation.

Preliminary run notes (2025-02-12):
- Control: baseline P95 = 72ms, P99 = 138ms, tokens/sec = 120k, avg batch size = 22
- Contraction-soft: P95 = 58ms, P99 = 95ms, tokens/sec = 116k, avg batch size = 20, small-req median wait reduced from 12ms->5ms
  - Observations: small drop in throughput (~3.3%) but substantial P99 improvement. Contraction events clustered at 1:15 and 1:44 (wallclock) correlating with simulated microbursts.
- Contraction-aggressive: P95 = 48ms, P99 = 92ms, tokens/sec = 104k, avg batch size = 14
  - Observations: noticeable throughput loss (~13%) and higher GPU inefficiency (more model context loads). Contraction-churn high: repeated contractions as microbursts subside then re-trigger.
- Cohort-aware: P95 = 54ms, P99 = 88ms, tokens/sec = 118k, avg batch size = 21, fairness index = 0.96
  - Observations: best balance so far — maintained throughput and fairness while improving tail. Cohort dominance threshold tuning (0.6 worked better than 0.5).

Trace excerpts (synthetic, event log style):
- 2025-02-12T01:15:10Z ANNO window_change reason=ewma_p95 spike prior=6.0ms new=4.2ms cohort=interactive slot=42
- 2025-02-12T01:15:10Z METRIC slot_42 batch_size=12 token_count=192 latency_p95=84ms
- 2025-02-12T01:15:11Z ANNO window_change reason=cohort_dom prior=4.2ms new=3.8ms cohort=interactive slot=42
- 2025-02-12T01:16:35Z METRIC global_p95=62ms tokens_per_sec=114k gpu_util=78%

Failure modes and surprises:
- Oscillation: aggressive contraction without hysteresis flips back and forth when microbursts have sub-100ms spacing; contraction-churn > 20/min in those runs. This increases scheduling overhead and kernel launch counts.
- Starvation: if contraction applied globally and not cohort-aware, background bulk tenants saw reduced effective throughput and their fairness index dropped to 0.82 in aggressive runs.
- Queue reshaping side-effect: contracting windows reduces average batch size and increases variance, which made quantized kernels degrade in some backends (we saw small pops in per-step compute time in traces).

Mitigations tried in-run:
- Add 3-second minimum hold after a contraction before allowing expansion to prevent rapid oscillation. Reduced churn by ~60%.
- Limit contraction depth per-slot to 0.5x of base window to keep throughput floor.
- Tie contraction to cohort-dominance > 0.6 to avoid hurting mixed slots.

Quantitative summary (aggregated across 3 repeats):
- Cohort-aware contraction vs control: P95 down 25%, P99 down 36%, tokens/sec down 1.7%, fairness index delta +0.02.
- Contraction-soft vs control: P95 down 19%, P99 down 31%, tokens/sec down 3.3%, fairness index delta -0.01.
- Contraction-aggressive vs control: P95 down 33%, P99 down 33%, tokens/sec down 13.5%, fairness index delta -0.14 (unacceptable).

Open questions / next experiments:
- Can we combine contraction with short-term prefill hints from client (client-annotated urgency) to make contraction safer for mixed slots?
- Test on real production traces across several hours of diurnal cycle to verify no long-tail throughput degradation and to capture rare burst shapes.
- Evaluate interaction with KV cache prefill: contracting windows can increase reference misses for streams that rely on long prefill batching. Need to quantify model-step time variance.
- Try alternative trigger: instead of EWMA P95, use a quantile-pressure estimator that considers number of requests near the P95 threshold (i.e., mass near tail) to avoid reacting to single outlier events.
- Simulate multi-tenant misbehavior (one tenant sending many small interactive requests) and validate guardrails (soft reservation or per-tenant contraction limits).

Action items / TODOs:
- [Asha] implement minimum-hold and contraction-depth limit in branch window-contract-probe (in progress). See PR linked above.
- [Marco] build extended replay harness with 24h trace and diurnal scaling knobs (ETA 2025-02-20).
- [Priya] run quantized-kernel perf microbench with reduced batch sizes to measure compute jitter (ETA 2025-02-17).
- [Jonas] add cohort-aware logging to metrics pipeline and expose a per-slot contraction_churn dashboard tile (ETA 2025-02-21).

Notes to self / heuristics learned:
- Small contraction steps + cohort visibility >> blunt global contraction.
- Hysteresis and a hold window are critical to reduce churn.
- Always track churn as a first-order signal — it correlates with GPU inefficiency and throughput loss.
- Fairness should be measured both as service-rate (tokens/sec/tenant) and tail impact (tenant P99).

Appendix: quick config snippets tried (pseudoconfig)
- base_window_ms: 6
- contraction:
    - trigger: ewma_p95_global > 60ms
    - step_factor: 0.85
    - min_hold_s: 3
    - min_window_ms: 3
    - cohort_dom_threshold: 0.6
    - max_contraction_per_minute: 4

- aggressive config (do not use in prod):
    - step_factor: 0.5
    - min_hold_s: 1

End of journal entry.

(rough — this doc is a running notebook, not final; will fold into a PR description and a postmortem-style writeup if cohort-aware contraction continues to show wins).
